bars.title: The player is never knocked around
bars.statement: In ten minutes of ordinary flight (no rope, no fields, no deliberate ram), contact changes the player's velocity ≤ 2 times per minute and never by more than 10 % of cruise in one event, never changes the player's heading, and never produces visible jitter; a deliberate big event (a slam the player chose, a well the player flew into) may, and it must be legible.
bars.target: ≤ 2 contact knocks per minute; largest ≤ 10 % of cruise; zero heading changes; no visible jitter

values.label: contact knocks per minute on the player, crucible (worst of 1 run(s))
largest single knock, fraction of cruise, crucible (worst of 1 run(s))
knock events that changed the player's heading, crucible (worst of 1 run(s))

bars.notes: visible jitter is unmeasured on this headless Crucible path; a full B13 pass is impossible. crucible knock counts come from short wave runs (~25 s of flight), not the contract's ten minutes of ordinary flight. the visible-jitter clause and the legible-deliberate-event clause are unbenched unless a headed capture sets jitterMeasured. the largest-knock ceiling is 0.1 of cruise compared with a tolerance of 0.000001: the live rule caps a contact event's cumulative applied delta-V at exactly that fraction, and the bench sums the per-receipt values in a different order, so a run that spends the whole budget lands one ulp above it. The tolerance is float slack, never headroom — at Kestrel cruise that is 0.0002 WU/s.

bars.notes: visible jitter on the flight bench has no pictures behind it: this evaluation carries no normal-speed Crucible strip whose frames measured jitter, so the clause stays open. the lateral-velocity sign-flip proxy (jitterEvents/jitterMaxSignFlips) is reported beside the clause and never folded into it. the visible-jitter clause and the legible-deliberate-event clause are unbenched unless a headed capture sets jitterMeasured. the largest-knock ceiling is 0.1 of cruise compared with a tolerance of 0.000001: the live rule caps a contact event's cumulative applied delta-V at exactly that fraction, and the bench sums the per-receipt values in a different order, so a run that spends the whole budget lands one ulp above it. The tolerance is float slack, never headroom — at Kestrel cruise that is 0.0002 WU/s.
